rules.title: Never swallow errors
rules.text: Never swallow exceptions silently; handle them, or rethrow with added context.

rules.title: Typed errors
rules.text: Use specific error types or codes instead of string matching on messages.

rules.title: Validate at boundaries
rules.text: Validate all external input (HTTP, files, env, user input) at the boundary and trust typed data inside.

rules.title: Fail fast on config
rules.text: Fail fast at startup when required configuration is missing or invalid.

rules.title: Safe user-facing messages
rules.text: Return safe user-facing error messages; keep stack traces and internals out of responses.

rules.title: Retry transient failures only
rules.text: Retry only transient failures and surface permanent failures immediately.

rules.title: Release resources
rules.text: Always release resources (files, connections, locks) in finally blocks or equivalent scopes.

rules.title: Avoid partial writes
rules.text: Make multi-step operations atomic or compensate on failure so state never stays half-updated.

rules.title: Convert errors at boundaries
rules.text: Translate low-level errors into domain errors at module boundaries.

rules.title: Assertions for invariants
rules.text: Use assertions only for programmer errors, never for validating input.

rules.title: Explicit absence
rules.text: Model absence explicitly (Option, nullable, Maybe) and avoid returning magic values like -1 or empty strings.

rules.title: Small try blocks
rules.text: Keep try blocks as small as possible and catch only exceptions the wrapped call can raise.

rules.title: Direct access after validation
rules.text: When validation guarantees a key exists, access it directly so contract violations fail loudly instead of being masked by defaults.

rules.title: Exhaustive switches
rules.text: Handle every expected case explicitly in switch and match statements. Reserve default for unexpected values and make it fail.
